reports.text: PA and lateral views. Cavitary lesion in the right upper lobe. Remaining lungs clear. No pleural effusion. Heart size normal. Mediastinum not widened.

documents.title: Pulmonology Consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside pulmonary clinic - consultation 01/06/2025, copy to primary care.

37-year-old man with HIV/AIDS, CKD stage 3, IgA nephropathy/FSGS, and an HIV-related skin infection under ID care, seen for three weeks of persistent cough with low-grade fevers, night sweats and about 10 pounds of weight loss. Increasingly tired. Antiretrovirals have been irregular again because of circumstances at home.

Meds as reported: bictegravir/emtricitabine/TAF, TMP-SMX, metformin, lisinopril, furosemide.
Allergies: NKDA. Smokes about 10 cigarettes daily.

Exam: T 38.2 C, HR 92, RR 20. Cachectic. Breath sounds diminished over the right upper lobe. No wheeze.

Data: CD4 180; viral load elevated per ID. Sputum AFB smear positive. Chest radiograph shows a cavitary lesion in the right upper lobe.

Impression: active pulmonary tuberculosis, smear-positive, cavitary.
Plan:
- Airborne precautions at home; mask.
- Reported to the state public health TB program for directly observed therapy; regimen to be coordinated with ID because of drug interactions with his antiretrovirals.
- Sputum cultures and susceptibilities pending.
- Follow-up here in 2 months.

documents.title: Pulmonology letter reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed pulmonology letter re active TB. Called pt - no answer; left message asking him to call, and that we want to see him once he's cleared to be around others. Called ID clinic: they are aware and coordinating with public health.

documents.title: TB Program Treatment Notice
documents.author: public health
documents.body:
State public health TB program - notice to primary care provider, dated 02/10/2025.

Re: Andre Palmer, DOB 10/24/1987.
Sputum culture from 01/06/2025 grew TB complex organisms, susceptible to isoniazid, rifampin, pyrazinamide and ethambutol.
Treatment: directly observed therapy started with isoniazid, rifabutin, pyrazinamide and ethambutol, with pyridoxine. Rifabutin chosen with the ID clinic, who adjusted his antiretroviral regimen for the interaction; details are in their records.
Please contact the program before prescribing new medications.

documents.title: Outreach call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called to check in and offer a visit; overdue for diabetes and kidney labs. Voicemail, message left with callback number. Pharmacy confirms metformin and lisinopril last filled in January.

documents.title: Gastroenterology Consultation
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside GI practice - consultation 07/08/2025.

Reason: painful swallowing.

37-year-old with AIDS, IgA nephropathy and FSGS, on treatment this year for pulmonary tuberculosis, with two weeks of pain on swallowing, about 10 pounds of weight loss and low-grade fevers. Antiretrovirals irregular. His HIV clinic gave him oral nystatin a week ago without improvement.

Allergies: no known drug allergies.

Exam: thin. Oral thrush on the tongue and palate. Abdomen soft, nontender.

Labs: hemoglobin 12.5, WBC 3.8, platelets 150K, CD4 50, HIV-1 RNA 120,000.

Impression: candidal esophagitis, presumed clinically given odynophagia with oral thrush and a CD4 of 50, failed topical therapy.
Plan:
- Fluconazole 200 mg once, then 100 mg daily for 21 days (dose reduced for kidney function); TB program and ID notified of the added drug.
- Endoscopy only if no response within 1 week.
- Restart and stay on antiretrovirals - ID to see him this month.

documents.title: TB Program Completion Notice
documents.author: public health
documents.body:
State public health TB program, 10/20/2025.
Andre Palmer has completed 9 months of directly observed therapy for drug-susceptible pulmonary tuberculosis. Treatment completed. Case closed with the program. Any new respiratory symptoms should prompt re-evaluation.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED - visit 01/19/2026.

CC: diarrhea.
HPI: 38M with AIDS and poor antiretroviral adherence, IgA nephropathy with FSGS, CKD 3; candidal esophagitis last July and pulmonary TB last year (treatment completed). Three weeks of watery diarrhea with about 10 lb weight loss. Denies fever, blood in stool, recent travel.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: mild diffuse abdominal tenderness without rebound or guarding. Mucous membranes dry.

Results: CD4 50. HIV-1 RNA 120,000. Stool culture: no Salmonella, Shigella or Campylobacter. Ova and parasites negative. Modified acid-fast stain of stool positive. C. difficile antigen negative.

ED course: IV fluids; tolerated oral fluids afterward.
Impression: cryptosporidiosis in advanced HIV, with dehydration.
Disposition: discharged home with oral rehydration instructions; ID clinic follow-up arranged within the week; antiretrovirals are the main treatment.

documents.title: ED follow-up call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called after ED record received. Spoke with pt briefly; diarrhea a little better, drinking fluids, saw ID on Friday. Offered visit here, he said he'd call when he's feeling better. Encouraged him to.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED - visit 04/06/2026.

CC: headache, fever, stiff neck.
HPI: 38M with AIDS (HIV for about five years, poor adherence), IgA nephropathy, CKD and cryptosporidiosis in January. Two weeks of headache, fever and neck stiffness, steadily worse despite acetaminophen.
Allergies: NKDA.

Vitals: T 38.5 C, BP 110/70, P 100, RR 18.
Exam: lethargic, oriented to person, place and time. Neck stiff; meningeal sign positive on passive neck flexion. No focal neurologic deficit.

Labs: WBC 4.5, Hgb 12.2, Plt 210K. CD4 50. HIV-1 RNA 120,000.
Lumbar puncture: opening pressure 280 mm H2O. CSF WBC 22/uL, 90% lymphocytes; protein 100 mg/dL; glucose 20 mg/dL. Ink preparation positive for encapsulated yeast. Cryptococcal antigen positive.

Impression: cryptococcal meningitis with raised intracranial pressure.
Disposition: admitted to medicine, ID consulted.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital - discharge summary.
Admitted 04/06/2026, discharged 04/21/2026.
Principal diagnosis: cryptococcal meningitis.
Other: AIDS (CD4 50), CKD with FSGS/IgA nephropathy, type 2 diabetes, hypertension.

Course: induction with liposomal amphotericin B and flucytosine for 2 weeks, doses adjusted to kidney function with daily labs. Repeat lumbar punctures to relieve pressure, with headache improving after each. Fever resolved and he became more alert.

Discharge medications: fluconazole 400 mg daily for 8 weeks, then 200 mg daily until ID says otherwise. Home medications otherwise as before.
Antiretrovirals: to be restarted at the ID clinic about 4 to 6 weeks after induction began.
Follow-up: ID clinic 1 week; primary care when able.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Checking in after your hospital stay
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Andre, I got the hospital summary. I'm glad you're home. Whenever you're ready, I'd like to see you - by video is fine - to go over your kidney and diabetes medicines with the new ones. Just reply here.

reports.text: Pre- and post-gadolinium imaging of the brain. Multiple ring-enhancing lesions in the cerebral cortex. No hemorrhage. Ventricles normal in size. No midline shift.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED - visit 07/21/2026.

CC: headache, fever, confusion.
HPI: 38M with AIDS and cryptococcal meningitis treated in April, brought in by his partner, who reports two weeks of worsening headache, fever and confusion; less responsive and having trouble walking.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: T 38.7 C. Neck stiff. Right-sided weakness.
Labs: CD4 50.
Imaging: MRI brain with multiple ring-enhancing lesions in the cerebral cortex.

Impression: cerebral toxoplasmosis.
Disposition: admitted to medicine, ID consulted.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital - discharge summary.
Admitted 07/21/2026, discharged 08/07/2026.
Principal diagnosis: cerebral toxoplasmosis.
Other: AIDS (CD4 50); cryptococcal meningitis (April 2026) on fluconazole; CKD with FSGS/IgA nephropathy; type 2 diabetes; hypertension.

Course: started pyrimethamine 200 mg once then 50 mg daily, sulfadiazine dosed to kidney function, and leucovorin 10 mg daily. Fever resolved; more alert day by day. Repeat MRI after 2 weeks showed the lesions smaller. Right-sided weakness improving with physical therapy.

Plan: complete 6 weeks of treatment, then maintenance per ID. Fluconazole continues. ID clinic in 1 week. Home with partner.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Call from partner
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt's partner called (pt on speaker, gave permission). Asking what follow-up he needs with us after the hospital. Offered next available video or office visit; partner wants to check the ID and PT schedule first and will call back. Hospital summary is in the chart for PCP.
